title: Degree is additive on tensor products of invertible modules on proper schemes of dimension at most one
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $X$ be a scheme proper over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism] of topological Krull dimension at most one [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], and let $\mathcal L,\mathcal M$ be invertible $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-sc-invertible-module]. With tensor product as in [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and degree $\deg_k(\mathcal F)=\chi(X,\mathcal F)-\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$ for an invertible module as in [def-pc-degree-line-bundle], one has $\deg_k(\mathcal L\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal M)=\deg_k(\mathcal L)+\deg_k(\mathcal M)$.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-proper-field-invertible-coherent], $X$ is Noetherian and $\mathcal L,\mathcal M,\mathcal O_X$ are coherent. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor], applied to $\mathrm{id}_X$, makes $\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal M$ invertible, so the same coherence result applies to it.

Apply [lem-trf-degree-weighted-irreducible-components] to $\mathcal L$, $\mathcal M$ and $\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal M$. All three use the same finite list of reduced integral one-dimensional components $j_i:C_i\to X$, proper over $k$, with the same finite weights $m_i$, since both the components and the weights depend only on $X$. Thus each degree is the sum of $m_i$ times the degree of its pullback to $C_i$. This formula already includes all of $X$: neither isolated zero-dimensional components nor embedded points add another term.

Put $L_i=j_i^*\mathcal L$ and $M_i=j_i^*\mathcal M$. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor] makes them invertible. Each $C_i$ is proper over $k$, so [lem-trf-proper-field-invertible-coherent] makes $M_i$ coherent. Apply [lem-trf-curve-pullback-tensor-euler] to $j_i$: $\chi(C_i,j_i^*(\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal M))=\deg_k(L_i)+\chi(C_i,M_i)$. Subtract $\chi(C_i,\mathcal O_{C_i})$ and use [def-pc-degree-line-bundle] to obtain $\deg_k(j_i^*(\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal M))=\deg_k(L_i)+\deg_k(M_i)$.

Substitute the component identity of Step 3 into the third sum in Step 2 and distribute the finite sum:
$$\deg_k(\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal M)=\sum_i m_i(\deg_k(L_i)+\deg_k(M_i))=\sum_i m_i\deg_k(L_i)+\sum_i m_i\deg_k(M_i)=\deg_k(\mathcal L)+\deg_k(\mathcal M).$$
All equalities are in $\mathbf Z$. If there are no dimension-one components, the three sums are empty and all three degrees are zero, so the same calculation applies, including $X=\varnothing$.

from.place: The fibrewise ampleness-to-projectivity argument: positivity on normalized geometric-fibre components is converted to relative ampleness and then to a projective-bundle embedding. Supporting input: the proper integral curve degree criterion (0B5X). In the 0B5X proof this is the tensor-product degree formula used to pass from the degree of a positive tensor power to the degree of the line bundle and to obtain linear Euler-characteristic growth.
